subject: Data classification, subprocessor list, and narrow-transfer language — MediSys privacy follow-up
messages:
From: Alex Todd <procurement@medisys.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: MediSys Health Legal <legal@medisys.com>
Date: 2026-11-15 09:12 -0800
Subject: Initial privacy questions — classification + subprocessors

Priyom,

Thanks for taking this call earlier. To keep the procurement loop moving we need a short written response on two points before Friday: a concise description of how PII from our integration is classified and stored (we asked about tokenization/anonymization during streaming vs. persistent storage), and an up-to-date list of subprocessors who might see unredacted content.

Two quick bullets we need answered for our Security & Privacy team:
- Do you persist raw user utterances outside of ephemeral KV caches? If so, under what retention policy and where (regions)?
- Which subprocessors (by company name) have potential access to decrypted PII, and do any subprocessors introduce cross-border transfer risk?

If you can attach any diagram that shows the runtime data flow (ingress, KV cache, long-term store, backups, KMS custody) that would be ideal. We may ask for a signed annex limiting transfers to our EU patient dataset, but first we need the technical detail.

Appreciate a short response—we have an internal review on Monday.

— Alex
Procurement, MediSys Health

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Todd <procurement@medisys.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-15 11:30 -0800
Subject: RE: Initial privacy questions — classification + subprocessors

Alex — thanks, this is helpful. Attached are three artifacts: a compact dataflow PDF (redwood-dataflow-v2.pdf), our canonical subprocessors CSV (subprocessor-list-2026.csv), and a short proposed DPA annex draft for your legal team's review (proposed-dpa-annex-draft.docx). Key answers below — short and actionable.

Summary answers:
- Persistence: Redwood does not persist raw user utterances by default. Runtime inference uses ephemeral KV cache on GPU hosts; cache entries are retained only for the session and are purged on eviction or session end. Long-term storage of generated content or transcripts happens only when a customer enables explicit logging/retention (API param or console toggle) and is then stored encrypted-at-rest per the retention period configured by the customer.
- Retention/regions: For customers who enable logging, stored artifacts are written to customer-specific buckets in the region you select. Default hosted storage regions are us-west-2, eu-west-1, and asia-southeast-1. Retention is configurable; standard template is 30 days, with options for 90/365 days on contract.
- Tokenization/anonymization: We provide optional client-side tokenization helpers in our SDKs and a server-side redaction integration that can be enabled for PII-sensitive endpoints. Redaction is configurable by field and leverages a Named Entity Recognition pipeline; this is an opt-in configuration per route.
- Subprocessors: the attached CSV lists subprocessors; the subset with potential access to decrypted PII (i.e., storage/KMS/managed ops) is: CloudStore Co., KeyGuard KMS (KMS-as-a-Service), GridOps Managed Services. All others have only telemetry/monitoring access to telemetry/metrics (no content access).
- Cross-border exposure: Our control plane may route requests for capacity to other regions for failover unless explicitly pinned. For customers requiring no transfers, we offer a VPC/private deployment (Redwood Private) and a contractual clause to restrict routing, plus a log-based attestation.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marcus and Hannah will add a short annex paragraph with suggested language to explicitly prohibit transfers of EU patient data outside EU unless explicit written approval is given.
2) Mina will prepare a signed KMS attestation snippet and list of HSM-backed key IDs that apply to your tenant if you want proof of custody.
3) If you need to proceed with the annex, please confirm which dataset(s) you want covered and we can generate a formal change order.

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood-dataflow-v2.pdf (diagram, 2 pages)] [Attachment: subprocessor-list-2026.csv (CSV, 1 page)] [Attachment: proposed-dpa-annex-draft.docx (Word, 3 pages)]

— Priyom
Head of Customer Privacy, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Todd <procurement@medisys.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-16 08:02 -0800
Subject: RE: Initial privacy questions — classification + subprocessors

Alex — looping in a few technical/controls items to make the DPA language specific enough for your reviewers. Quoting Priyom below for context. Short bullets we recommend including in the annex (draft language available on request):

- Narrow transfer clause: "Redwood shall not transfer, process, or permit access to MediSys Health EU Patient Data outside the EEA without prior written consent from MediSys Health, except as required by law."
- KMS custody: we use customer-specific key material for Private deployments and can provide per-tenant HSM-wrapped keys for Dedicated plans. For hosted customers, KeyGuard KMS is used; keys are tenant-scoped and we can provide a KMS attestation certificate for the key IDs listed in the attachment.
- Access control/least privilege: long-term storage buckets containing logged transcripts are accessible only to a named ops role by default; access is logged and requires a justification and two-step approval for decryption actions.
- Emergency access & audit: we can provide time-bound emergency access only with prior approvals and will include audit logs and a notification window (usually 24 hours) to the customer's security contact.

I also attach an ops checklist that shows who in Redwood can request decryption and the on-call flow. If MediSys needs, we can redact the checklist into a short attestation letter for procurement.

On the cross-border question: if you want to guarantee no routing to non-EU GPUs, the clean path is a Private (VPC) or Dedicated EU-only deployment; otherwise we can add explicit contractual routing constraints plus an automated policy to prefer EU capacity.

— Marcus
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed-dpa-annex-draft.docx (updated suggestions)]

From: Alex Todd <procurement@medisys.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: MediSys Health Legal <legal@medisys.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-17 16:05 -0800
Subject: RE: Initial privacy questions — classification + subprocessors

Thanks — that was fast and thorough. A couple follow-ups from legal and our security reviewer:

1) Legal: please prepare the annex with the narrow transfer clause Marcus suggested. We will review and come back with any redlines but this is promising.
2) Security: can you provide the KMS attestation (Mina) and a sample of the audit log format for decryption events? We need to ingest that into our SIEM parsers.

If you can get the annex and the two evidence items into DocuSign or a shared Box folder by EOD Monday, we can aim to be contract-ready in the same week. Also, please flag whether there are any subprocessors in the attached CSV that you expect to sunset in the next 90 days — our vendor team wants to avoid follow-up churn.

Appreciate it — Alex
Procurement, MediSys Health
